{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the sales data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue to numeric, coercing errors to NaN
# The value '999,999.99' is likely a sentinel for missing or invalid data
# We'll treat it as NaN

# First, inspect the revenue column again to confirm the format
df['revenue_clean'] = pd.to_numeric(df['revenue'].str.replace(',', ''), errors='coerce')

# Check for any non-numeric values after cleaning
print('After conversion, NaN count in revenue_clean:', df['revenue_clean'].isna().sum())

# Review the rows where revenue is NaN
print('\nRows with NaN revenue:')
print(df[df['revenue_clean'].isna()][['order_id', 'revenue']])

# Check the status column for these rows
print('\nStatus of rows with NaN revenue:')
print(df[df['revenue_clean'].isna()]['status'].value_counts())"}
